page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, which operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. It contains no local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable, and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2701.97. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% with a stress-ng score of 5398.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3667.0. Memory bandwidth is average for large block read-only operations at 41.63 GB/sec, but weak for small block cached reads at 259.4 GB/sec and large block writes at 24.61 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile, the D4as_v5 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not demand heavy multi-threaded processing or local disk storage. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded applications. However, database operations and high-throughput static web serving are constrained, as indicated by weak Passmark database and Redis SET benchmark results. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware provides a stable baseline for entry-level enterprise workloads, though resource-intensive multi-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference will encounter performance bottlenecks.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage, though it supports Premium Storage. Benchmarks show a clear performance tradeoff: single-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%, while multi-core CPU performance and memory write bandwidth fall into the bottom 25%. Single-threaded compression and image processing tasks perform at average levels, but multi-threaded decompression and database operations are weak. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, lightweight web serving, and text processing tasks that rely on single-core execution rather than dense parallel processing or high-throughput local storage.
